# Content Calendar Planning

`content-calendar-planning` · v1.1.0 · Execute · Content & Copy
<!-- Generated by platform/scripts/generate-engine-specs.mjs from skills/content-calendar-planning/spec.json and SKILL.md. Do not edit. -->

**Decision it supports:** Can our team actually keep this content calendar, and what should we cut to make it fit?

**Inputs:** Audience/personas, business goals, target topics or keywords, publishing capacity, and channels

**Output:** A capacity feasibility verdict, a topic-cluster plan with authority scoring, a dated publishing schedule, and a repurposing flow from each core asset to social

**Setup:**
- Install the skill: `npx skills add sarojkjha/aaj-marketing-skills --skill content-calendar-planning`
- Or connect the hosted MCP server, no install: `https://aaj-engines-mcp.sarojkjha10.workers.dev/mcp`
- Or run the local MCP server: node platform/mcp/server.mjs (Node 18 or newer)
- Input schema: the comment at the top of `skills/content-calendar-planning/resources/calendar-engine.js` (the MCP server's describe_engine shows it). Worked example: `node skills/content-calendar-planning/resources/calendar-engine.js --demo`.
- Agents listed: Claude Code, Cursor, OpenAI Codex, Windsurf, Cline. Tested and recorded: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex (Windows, ab-test-significance only).

**Acts or analyzes:** Analyzes only. The engine makes no network calls, writes no files and changes nothing in your tools; it returns text and JSON.

**Where your information goes:**

| How you run it | Where your inputs go |
|---|---|
| Skill installed in your agent, or the local MCP server | The engine runs on your machine and AAJ receives nothing. Your AI agent still sends what you give it to its model provider (Anthropic, OpenAI and so on), under your own account's terms. |
| Hosted MCP server | Your agent's model provider, as above, plus AAJ's server on Cloudflare, which receives the engine inputs over HTTPS, runs them in memory and keeps no copy. Cloudflare keeps error logs (no inputs) for up to 7 days. |

No engine needs customer names, emails or other personal data; leave them out.

**Limitations:**
- Hours come from fixed format defaults (pillar 12, blog 5, post 0.5 and so on). If your pieces take longer, override them with effort, or the plan looks more feasible than it is.
- It checks capacity, cluster structure and timing, not topic choice. It cannot tell whether a cluster targets real demand or will rank.
- Time to impact assumes a fixed ramp from publish to contribution, four months by default. That is an assumption to set, not a forecast for your site.
- Cluster authority is a count: a pillar with fewer than three supporting pieces is flagged. It does not judge the quality of the pieces or how they interlink.

**Review before acting:** The content lead confirms contributor hours and per-format effort match how long pieces really take, and the founder confirms the goal date, before the schedule is committed.

Method: [skills.aajconsult.com/skills/content-calendar-planning](https://skills.aajconsult.com/skills/content-calendar-planning)
